title: Adaptive ingress/egress sliding minimums with enterprise SQ preflight
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: run a bounded experiment to validate an adaptive per-token model that separates ingress (input) and egress (output) tokens, applies a sliding-window minimum for streaming sessions, and exposes a discount schedule for high-frequency burst behavior. Also complete a preflight of the enterprise security questionnaire (SQ) and contract clauses needed if we surface directionally split metering to enterprise customers.

Background: many customers request asymmetric billing because in retrieval-heavy flows, input tokens can dominate costs; conversely, generation-heavy flows drive egress. Current hosted API billing is single per-token or IO-split experiments that assume static floors. This ticket tests a sliding minimum that adapts to session behavior (e.g., short bursts vs long conversational sessions), plus an enterprise-facing SQ/contract checklist so sales/legal can approve pilot deals without lengthy redlines.

Success criteria: 1) accuracy of per-token cost alignment: measured reduction in unit-cost variance across 10 pilot customers (target: 15% variability reduction). 2) Customer acceptance: pilot NPS >= 60 for billing clarity and 3) operational viability: no more than 2% increase in billing infra latency and audit logs completeness for SQ review.

Experiment design: we will implement two billing variants and sample customers into them: A) Sliding-minimum window (30-minute decay) with directional IO split weights (input 0.6 / output 0.4 baseline) and burst credit buffer that caps minimums for first N sessions; B) Session-anchored microfloor where the minimum is computed per user-session class (short <60s, mid 60-600s, long >600s) and decays per-session after inactivity. Both variants include a streaming discount ladder applied to egress tokens after 100k tokens/session.

Instrumentation: billing logs must include token direction, session id, window start/end, floor applied, burst credit consumed, and canonicalized prompt hash for cost repro. We will push telemetry to billing-sim_v2 dashboard and tag telemetry as pm/PM-777210 for easy aggregation.

Legal / Enterprise SQ work: compile a contract appendix that: (1) defines directional unit definitions and examples; (2) enumerates auditability guarantees (per-request token logs retained 90 days by default with enterprise option to extend); (3) provides fallback wording for disputes and rounding rules; (4) includes an opt-in clause for pilot customers. Create a short SQ response bundle (answers + artifact links) for Security Review and Sales preflight.

Risk & mitigations: Billing confusion risk — mitigate with clear invoice samples and pre-pilot onboarding sessions. Technical risk — we will run billing computation in the billing-sim pipeline first (offline) before switching live metering. Legal risk — pre-approve appendix with Legal and Security; require manual sign-off for each pilot.

notes: Trade-offs discussed: fixed floors are simpler but penalize burst-y apps; sliding windows add billing complexity and require strong invoice UX. We prioritized a 30-minute decay as a midpoint and selected 100k token egress threshold to keep discounts focused on very heavy streams. Engineering will validate ledger idempotency under the new window model.
